device_template.name: Huawei SUN2000 inverter
device_template.author: Stefan Maldaianu
device_template.description: Huawei SUN2000 string or hybrid inverter over Modbus TCP (SDongle or the inverter's WLAN) or Modbus RTU, read-only: identity 30000-30076 (model, serial, PN, firmware, strings, MPPTs, rated and maximum power), the State 1/2/3 and Alarm 1/2/3 bit fields at 32000-32010, PV1-PV8 voltage and current from 32016, the AC block 32064-32094 (input power, line and phase voltages and currents, active and reactive power, PF, frequency, efficiency, internal temperature, insulation, device status, fault code, startup/shutdown time) and the total (32106) and daily (32114) yield, served in Wh. Big-endian, high word first. The DTSU666 meter and the LUNA2000 battery behind the inverter have their own templates (huawei_dtsu666_via_sun2000, huawei_luna2000): add them as further devices on the same connection and unit ID, only where the site has them. PV5-PV8 are a separate read, so a model with four strings that refuses them does not lose PV1-PV4. Field notes: enable Modbus TCP on the SDongle in FusionSolar (Dongle parameters -> Modbus TCP -> Enable unrestricted); unit ID = the inverter's RS485 address (usually 1); the dongle serves ONE Modbus client only, so keep a single gateway connection and poll every 10-30 s; port 502 on the SDongle, 6607 on the inverter's own WLAN access point; Modbus RTU direct on the inverter's RS485 is 9600 8N1. The inverter is the master of its RS485 bus to the DTSU666 meter: never add a second master there, use the listen-only rtu_tap mode to watch it. SunSpec (40000) is a quick alternative without battery, meter or alarms.
device_template.source_document: Huawei 'Solar Inverter Modbus Interface Definitions' (Huawei SUN2000 Modbus interface, register 30000-32114 tables, device status codes, State/Alarm bit fields); cross-read against wlcrs/huawei-solar-lib register definitions. Not yet checked on hardware.

pv_extra.description: PV5-PV8, a read of their own (absent on smaller models)

normal.description: state and alarm bit fields, status, fault, temperature, efficiency

static.description: identity strings, strings/MPPT count, rated power

notes.text: Not yet checked on hardware: compare AC power, the PV strings and the yield with FusionSolar or the inverter app before relying on them. The alarm bit names and the status list follow Huawei's interface definitions.
The SDongle serves one Modbus TCP client. A second client (another gateway, Home Assistant) makes both drop out. Poll every 10-30 s; faster polling makes the dongle answer late or not at all.

Setup: FusionSolar -> the SDongle -> Dongle parameters -> Modbus TCP -> Enable (unrestricted). Port 502 on the SDongle, 6607 on the inverter's own WLAN. Unit ID = the inverter's RS485 address, usually 1. RTU direct: 9600 8N1.
If a read answers 'illegal data address' (a register this model does not have), set the device's max gap to 0 or list the address in its illegal registers: the other values keep reading.

The inverter is the master of its RS485 bus to the DTSU666 meter. Never add a second master on that bus; watch it with the listen-only rtu_tap mode. SunSpec (40000) is a quicker alternative, without battery, meter or alarms.
